experience.title: Principal Software Engineer
experience.scope: Architecture and data-model owner across the commercial platform; squad lead for four engineers; named tech lead on invoicing, a field-operations product and legacy product support; guides ~10 engineers across several teams.
highlights: Platform architecture: own architecture across 12+ domain services behind one API gateway — service boundaries, data models and the specifications the team builds from; JWT verification and per-route rate limiting solved once at the edge.

Live database migration: directed a live MySQL-to-PostgreSQL migration across six product lines with no maintenance window — re-runnable historical backfill separated from a continuous reverse-sync so unmigrated products kept serving; specified ID mapping, idempotency, retries, monitoring and rollback in ~25,000 words executed by other engineers. Zero customer-visible incidents.
Finance-auditable billing: designed a discount engine with a four-tier approval ladder (self-approval to C-suite), rack-rate vs selling-price handling, and date-derived contract terms.
Invoicing tech lead: designed oldest-invoice-first payment mapping with structured proof-of-payment capture to cut reconciliation lag against a DSO target.

Peak reliability: re-architected a blocking annual batch path into asynchronous per-activity events, holding 99.9% uptime through the academic-year peak; built queue-driven order-to-access activation/deactivation.

Technical leadership: set review, testing and coding standards in business-critical modules; coach on defect prevention and root-cause analysis; monthly programme status to leadership for 7+ consecutive months.

systems_owned.name: Order & subscription platform
systems_owned.summary: SKU-based catalogue with bundle suggestion by grade and subject, rules-engine discounting, finance-auditable premium pricing, multi-year orders, invoicing, and the activation keys that become a student's subscription.

systems_owned.name: MySQL to Postgres, live
systems_owned.summary: Two-way bridge between a fifteen-year-old MySQL estate and new Postgres microservices. Dual-write, reconciliation, and a mapping spec precise enough that someone else could run the cutover. Migrated by domain, not by table, so each cutover was independently reversible. Lesson: instrument reconciliation earlier.

systems_owned.name: API gateway & aggregation
systems_owned.summary: One gateway fronting 12+ domain services: JWT auth, request validation, rate limiting, Redis caching, retrying upstream clients, structured logging.

systems_owned.name: Multi-role authorisation / IAM
systems_owned.summary: Users → groups → organisations, scoped consistently across services, including users holding several roles at once and ownership overrides surviving every query path.

systems_owned.name: Visits, evidence, retention
systems_owned.summary: GPS-verified check-in, S3 document capture, contribution to speech-to-text and visit-summary design, DPDP-compliant retention built in rather than retrofitted.

systems_owned.name: CRM, finance, HR
systems_owned.summary: Third-party systems behind ports and adapters so a vendor can be swapped without touching a caller; bounded-concurrency scheduled syncs above the gateway.

projects.name: Automated code-review pipeline
projects.summary: Scheduled agent pipeline (TypeScript, Node.js, MCP) that reviews open Bitbucket pull requests unattended on a 30-minute cadence and publishes a triaged report per repository — 6-dimension quality matrix, evidence-based findings with file + line, severity-gated inline comments, approve/needs-fix verdict. Always reads the linked Jira ticket first.

projects.summary: Reviews Bitbucket PRs against a configurable standard, with a provider abstraction over hosted and local models so a team picks its own cost/latency/privacy trade-off.

projects.name: Engineering-ops automation skills
projects.summary: A set of reusable agent skills built for the squad: PR inbox (open PRs by author/reviewer), PR review, build-release email generation from Jira fix-versions, sprint/monthly squad briefings from Jira + Confluence, personal sprint retrospectives, Jira ticket creation from conversation, and an actionable-email rewriter for system alerts.

leadership_philosophy: Write the specification, then review against it — make the disagreement happen before the code exists, when it is cheap.
Code review is where teaching happens — the main quality surface and the main development surface at once; built an AI reviewer to take the mechanical half off people's plates.
Guiding ten is different from managing one — influence at that width comes from the artefacts you leave behind: specs, schemas, review comments, service boundaries.
